\subsection{Retrieval source: open web versus the data lake}
\label{sec:web-arm}

To test whether the retrieval axis reflects the data lake specifically or
a more general property of the agent, we replaced lake search with
open-web search. The arm uses the Parallel Search API and, under
\texttt{-{}-no-s3}, loses every lake-backed file tool: the agent keeps only
\texttt{download}, which fetches an arbitrary \texttt{http(s)} URL into its
sandbox, and \texttt{execute\_code}. All arms hold the remaining axes at
\texttt{search\_results=naive}, \texttt{profile=standard} and
\texttt{computation\_tool=standard}, since the ideal computation tools
resolve against authored data-lake records and would make a web run's
outcome independent of what it retrieved. Each arm was run three times.

The web arm reaches 38.3\% against 56.7\% for the
strongest lake arm, a gap of 18.3\,pp that clears the
$\pm12$\,pp two-sigma replicate threshold measured across these arms.

The more informative quantity is where retrieval breaks down.
$D_{ret}$ is the fraction of gold datasets that appeared in search
results; $D_{acc}$ is the fraction the agent actually read.
All three lake arms surface gold at a similar rate (Ideal 82.5\%, Standard 84.1\%, Naive 85.6\%), so they
are not separated by what search returns. They are separated by the
drop between finding and reading (Ideal 3.4\,pp, Standard 16.2\,pp, Naive 15.7\,pp): oracle search wins because
the agent acts on what it was shown, not because it was shown more.

For the web arm both quantities are undefined rather than zero: it
touches no lake datasets by construction, so it can neither retrieve nor
read a gold source.

\paragraph{What the web arm actually measures.}
\texttt{download} accepts any URL, and the model routinely constructs one
from pretrained knowledge rather than following a search result: live
Socrata queries against \texttt{data.cityofnewyork.us}, \texttt{data.va.gov}
export endpoints, and a timestamped \texttt{web.archive.org} URL. The arm
therefore measures an agent with open web access and code execution, not
web-search retrieval, and its data path may be stronger than the lake
arms' since it aggregates live authoritative sources rather than a fixed
snapshot. That liveness also produces false negatives: two failures were
arithmetically correct against current data but disagreed with gold
answers derived from the snapshot (2{,}700{,}968 against a gold
2{,}705{,}988; 2923.59 against 2941).
